'Good developer' is dependent on the kind of work you are going to do. If your job is to develop a web based front-end (web application for example) having a good understanding of HTML, CSS and Javascript certainly goes a long way. I would also at least get a bit of experience with things like SASS or LESS (they really help!). You could also look at Jade (in my opinion a lot cleaner than plain HTML). Instead of Javascript also give Typescript a try just to experience the benefits of strong-typing (just to name one of the benefits). Of course if you are going this route an automatic build system is required so also look at Grunt and/or Gulp.

Like I said HTML, CSS and Javascript goes a long way but there are a lot of other technologies which can really help you develop faster/better/less buggy/etc. websites.

Frameworks are a bit of a touchy subject. There are a lot of Javascript frameworks out there making it impossible to learn them all. Programmers are also really passionate when it comes to their favorite framework (or the one they hate). My advice would be to experiment with a couple of the popular ones and pick the ones you like best. Google can help (just type something like "angular vs" and watch the results) but remember that in the end you must make the decision yourself.

If however you are also expected to build a back-end you're going to have to look at languages like PHP, C# or any programming language usable for server side programming. NodeJS might be interesting seeing how it is basically Javascript usable for back-end applications.

Of course there are tons of interesting technologies/languages I did not mention here (because I forgot or am not yet familiar with them) so I am very interested in what other people recommend.

If those are the languages you're familiar with I suggest you install Greasemonkey (for Firefox) or Tampermonkey (for Chrome) and try some hacks on Javascript. There is a lot you can do with that, here is the userscript I'm currently using: http://pastebin.com/eTsbUq7r

Then when you're ready for the next step you can start hacking the Voat API. The new API is currently being tested and is not yet available for the site but it works well - this will give you plenty of time to play with user-scripts until it's officialy released https://voat.co/v/voatdev/comments/88531

Feel free to send a message if you ever need a quick help!

IMO you can get pretty far with JavaScript as your only programming language these days. With Node.js, you can effectively put together an entire web project without writing a single line of any other programming language.

I think you're sort of asking the wrong question, however. Being a good developer doesn't depend on what language you use. It depends on how you approach & solve problems. Interpreted languages are all reasonably similar, so if you know JavaScript, the barrier to entry for Python or Ruby or whatever else is relatively low. The bigger issue if you only do frontend UI work is that you aren't exposed to a very wide variety of problems to solve. Doing backend work will probably require you at some point to deal with a variety of new challenges like database modeling, system calls, queues, distribution, etc., but all of these challenges can still be tackled using JavaScript & Node.js.
